person.name: Ishank Bahl
person.headline: Senior Software Engineer and Tech Lead
person.positioning: Seven years building product end to end, from micro-frontends and design systems to the APIs, data models and infrastructure underneath.

intro: I work on the parts of a system other teams depend on. That has meant a hierarchical configuration model and a React micro-frontend that had to live inside an Angular host, the home and discovery surfaces of a streaming product, and the feature flag SDK that server side experiments call.

I write the services and data models behind those interfaces too, in Node, Python and SQL, and I have owned the infrastructure they run on. The work is the contract underneath the screen rather than the screen: what a team can change safely, what breaks when they do, and who finds out.

selectedWork.problem: Configuration was flat, with no way to express a default at one level and an override at another, and a new React surface had to ship inside an Angular application nobody was going to rewrite.
selectedWork.whatIBuilt: I designed the hierarchical configuration model and the resolution order that decides which level wins, then integrated a React micro-frontend into the Angular host through Module Federation so the two could release on separate cycles. I also built the Slack assistant that reads on-call context and drafts triage and patch steps.
selectedWork.decision: I put the React surface behind Module Federation rather than rebuilding it as an Angular component. The two applications ship independently now. It cost a shared dependency contract that has to be kept in step, and a second build to reason about when production breaks.

selectedWork.problem: Home and discovery carried a growing set of trays, each built its own way, so every new one started near scratch and behaved slightly differently from the last.
selectedWork.whatIBuilt: I led the continue watching tray, the watchlist tray and the details overlay, then pulled what they had in common into platform components the rest of home and discovery were built from. It is the first screen of every session, so a regression there is not a quiet one.
selectedWork.decision: I made the tray components take their data already shaped instead of letting each one fetch and normalise its own. That removed a class of inconsistency between trays. It cost a coordination step: adding a tray means touching the layer that assembles the data, not dropping a component in.

selectedWork.problem: VWO could experiment on the frontend but not behind an API, so anything decided on the server was untestable.
selectedWork.whatIBuilt: I co-wrote the Node SDK, the library an application calls to evaluate a flag and report which variation a user got, and wrote the frontend architecture for the product around it. It is Apache 2.0 on GitHub with my name in the authors list, so this is the one card here whose code you can read.
selectedWork.decision: We kept one package serving both the server and the browser instead of splitting it in two. One behaviour to document and test. It cost the browser build a size budget the server never needed, which is why that repo carries a gzipped size badge.
